title: RCMP forced to shoot fake gun-wielding man, judge says
subtitle: Fatality inquiry report into death of Canmore robbery suspect in 2011 has no recommendations
article: A provincial court judge makes no recommendations in his report about a fatal RCMP shooting in Canmore.
Jean Steven Boucher, 63, was shot by two RCMP officers in January 2011 as they tried to arrest him in the mountain town west of Calgary.
Boucher was suspected of robbing several businesses at gunpoint in the days leading up to the shooting, the inquiry heard.
According to testimony, Boucher pointed a replica of a Smith & Wesson 45-calibre handgun at the two arresting officers.
They reacted by firing at Boucher 11 times, striking him three times, killing him instantly.
Provincial court Judge Peter Barley said the officers had no other option than to use lethal force.
The officers acted in accordance with their training, common sense and the Criminal Code of Canada, he said.
